substitution_attempted: No attempt was made because the work was assigned to the individual personally and required client-specific system access.
decides_what_work_and_what_order: The client’s operations coordinator assigns the tickets and sets their priority. The worker can choose the order of minor tasks within the daily queue.
decides_how_work_performed: The worker uses their own professional judgment about how to complete each task, subject to the client’s quality and security procedures.
hours_and_location_set: Core hours are agreed in advance, generally 9:00 to 17:30 on weekdays. Work is performed remotely, with occasional attendance at the client’s office requested for team meetings.
report_to_a_manager: The worker reports to the service delivery manager and attends a short Monday planning call. Performance issues are discussed directly with that manager.
defective_work_corrected: The worker is expected to correct errors without additional payment where the error is attributable to them. The client supplies access and information needed for the correction.
loss_on_engagement: There is little practical opportunity to make a loss because the worker is paid for approved hours. Unpaid rework can reduce the effective hourly return.
presented_as_part_of_organisation: The worker uses a client email address and appears in the internal support directory. Customers are generally told they are part of the client’s service team.
staff_benefits_training_management: The worker receives mandatory security training and is supervised through the client’s ticketing system. They do not receive holiday pay, pension contributions, or other staff benefits.
practical_bar: The contract requires the worker to obtain approval before taking other paid work during scheduled hours. Other engagements are theoretically possible outside those hours, but the approval requirement is a practical restriction.

substitution_attempted: The worker sent a qualified colleague to cover two weeks of planned leave. The client accepted the substitute after receiving a short résumé and proof of insurance.
decides_what_work_and_what_order: The worker agrees a deliverable list with the client but decides which design tasks to tackle first. The client can reject additions outside the agreed scope.
decides_how_work_performed: The worker chooses the software, workflow, and creative method without day-to-day instruction. The client specifies brand requirements and the final approval standard.
hours_and_location_set: There are no fixed hours, and the worker works mainly from a private studio. Occasional site visits are arranged by mutual agreement when measurements or photographs are needed.
report_to_a_manager: There is no line manager. The worker speaks with the client’s marketing lead about milestones, but the relationship is project-based rather than supervisory.
defective_work_corrected: The worker bears the cost of correcting work that fails the agreed brief because of their error. Changes caused by a new client preference are quoted separately.
loss_on_engagement: The worker can make a loss if revisions take longer than estimated or if subcontracting costs exceed the fixed fee. They also pay for software, studio overhead, and travel.
presented_as_part_of_organisation: The worker is identified to third parties as an external design studio and uses their own trading name. They are not listed on the client’s staff directory.
staff_benefits_training_management: No staff benefits or internal training are provided. The worker manages their own schedule and may use a substitute without routine supervision.
practical_bar: The worker routinely serves several clients at the same time. The agreement contains no restriction on taking other commissions.

substitution_attempted: A substitute was proposed when the worker was unwell, but the client required its own interview and would only accept someone already familiar with the client’s systems. The proposed substitute was therefore not used.
decides_what_work_and_what_order: The client’s shift supervisor allocates tasks at the start of each shift and can move the worker between stations. The worker has no meaningful control over the order of work.
decides_how_work_performed: The client sets the operating method through written procedures and close on-site instruction. The worker can make minor practical adjustments but must follow the supervisor’s directions.
hours_and_location_set: The client publishes a rota and sets the workplace at its distribution depot. Shifts can be changed by the supervisor with limited notice.
report_to_a_manager: The worker reports to the shift supervisor and signs in through the depot attendance system. Absences must be reported to that supervisor before the shift begins.
defective_work_corrected: The worker repeats inaccurate stock counts during paid time. The client bears the cost of ordinary operational correction, although deliberate misconduct may lead to disciplinary action.
loss_on_engagement: The worker cannot normally make a financial loss from the engagement because equipment and consumables are supplied by the client. The main risk is losing future shifts.
presented_as_part_of_organisation: The worker wears the client’s branded high-visibility vest and is introduced to drivers as a depot operative. They use the same access badge and internal procedures as permanent staff.
staff_benefits_training_management: The client provides induction, manual-handling training, and daily supervision. The worker does not receive the full benefits package available to permanent employees.
practical_bar: Other work is possible on non-rostered days, although the unpredictable rota makes regular outside work difficult. The worker has occasionally accepted weekend shifts elsewhere.

substitution_attempted: No attempt was made because the worker chose to complete the installation personally and had already scheduled the work around other contracts.
decides_what_work_and_what_order: The worker receives a broad statement of requirements and independently plans the survey, procurement, and installation stages. The client only sets the required completion date.
decides_how_work_performed: The worker determines the technical method and selects suitable materials within the agreed budget. The client may inspect the finished installation but does not direct the process.
hours_and_location_set: The worker chooses the hours and attends whichever properties are included in the work order. Access appointments with occupants are coordinated with the client but can be rearranged by the worker.
report_to_a_manager: There is no manager or regular reporting line. The worker sends progress updates at agreed milestones and raises technical questions only when necessary.
defective_work_corrected: The worker must return at their own expense to remedy installation defects covered by the warranty. If the defect arises from faulty client-supplied materials, the client pays for the additional visit.
loss_on_engagement: A fixed price creates a genuine risk of loss if materials, travel, or remedial visits cost more than expected. The worker also carries vehicle and tool expenses.
presented_as_part_of_organisation: The worker trades under the name North Quay Field Services and gives customers their own business card. They are presented as an independent contractor rather than as part of the client’s workforce.
staff_benefits_training_management: The worker receives no benefits, internal training, or supervision. They maintain their own certifications and decide whether to hire assistance.
practical_bar: The worker actively performs similar installations for several other clients. The agreement expressly permits concurrent contracts provided deadlines are met.

substitution_attempted: The worker asked to send an assistant for one afternoon, but the client refused because only the named worker had completed its onboarding. No further substitution was attempted.
decides_what_work_and_what_order: The client provides a weekly list of research assignments and sets the order where deadlines overlap. The worker can arrange the detailed sequence of interviews and desk research.
decides_how_work_performed: The worker selects the research techniques and drafts the reports independently. The client’s project lead reviews methodology at checkpoints and may require changes to the reporting format.
hours_and_location_set: The agreement states a target of 24 hours per week, but the worker chooses when to perform them within agreed availability windows. Most work is remote, with one client-site meeting each fortnight.
report_to_a_manager: The worker reports to a project lead for deliverables and attends fortnightly review meetings. There is no formal disciplinary chain, though missed deadlines are escalated to the account director.
defective_work_corrected: The worker must revise reports that contain avoidable errors without charging extra. The client pays separately for revisions caused by changed assumptions or a materially expanded brief.
loss_on_engagement: The worker is paid partly by milestone, so extensive rework can reduce the return on their time. Ordinary business costs are modest, and the contract does not require purchase of specialist equipment.
presented_as_part_of_organisation: The worker is shown on selected project materials as an external research consultant and retains a separate email signature. Internally they have access to the client’s collaboration platform but are not included in staff announcements.
staff_benefits_training_management: The client provides a short systems induction and reviews deliverables, but no employee benefits are provided. Supervision is limited to project coordination rather than continuous management.
practical_bar: The worker can take other engagements, although the weekly availability commitment limits overlapping deadlines. They have completed two small projects for other clients during this period.
